Ugu Water Woes

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What is going on in Ugu that peope are without water repeatedly, for years on end?

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche has been receiving submissions from the people of the South Coast area for several years - Ugu District Municipality covers 4 local municipalities on the KZN South Coast. The entire region has been plagued by water service delivery issues for years. As far back as 2015, residents began complaining about regular water cuts, a high number of water service interruptions and the Ugu Municipality's lack of engagement with them. Now it's time for answers.

CURRENTLY Some 28 000 households which receive their water from the Umthamvuna Water Treatment Works have not had a reliable supply for the past month. According to the Ugu Municipality, the pump was damamged during the floods over Easter, but the community says these problems have been around for a long time.

Summary:
TREATMENT Either start with the most dramatic case study of a business or family out of water…or link about submissions to CB -- (reading complains excerpts from the FB page and letters we have received)..Film the rest like a bit of a travelogue...show where the place is and what the importance of the area is – Gautengers know it as the beach capital of the Easter holidays…LINK – We've been watching the story closely, hundreds of complaints and we've decided to pay a visit to the KZN South Coast -- presenter driving to South Coast…Drone shots.
Dave Watson / George Henderson, DA councillors who have been assisting the community for the past 4 years, by keeping people in the loop. They post daily or weekly updates on FB letting people know what's going on, where the outages are and where to find tankers with relief water, if there are any...
They can outline the issues... explain the problems.. They can take us to the water reservoirs explain how they're repeatedly running dry...
Visit & speak to residents and business owners about frustrations – from Hibberdene to Port Edward
Anthony Turton (Or he might refer me to expert with closer knowledge) on the aging of infrastructure, the issue with saltwater in the system... Show footage of the river and pumping station Additional issues like sewage spills and infrastructure failing etc (have footage of spills and water leaks)
Ugu Municipality – DD Naidoo is the Municipal Manager, but I'm not sure he will concede to an interview... So we'll doorstop the municipality
Auditor General on irregularities in the Ugu financials
Have footage of many water leaks on the coast
Have pictures of dirty water from the taps
Below are just some “highlights” - there are literally daily reports of no water on the South Coast, and of water leaks and burst pipes.

Further information:
HIGHLIGHTS
Experts say that salt water entered the water system during the drought in 2015 – which has corroded pipes and caused the collapse of the already aging infrastructure – Nov 2015 – complaints of salty water and brown water coming out of taps
UGU issues tender for R17Million for security services for 36 months (should cover the 2 strikes and sabotage, however no-one ever saw security company anywhere)
Dec 2016 – Water Crisis... lot of areas without water for more than a week – December holidays – SAMWU strike blamed
Feb 2016 – places report 6 days no water
Sept 2017 – Water Crisis – lack of water for more than 11 days
Jul 2017 – School Holidays – water shortages – Municipality issues a statement
Nov 2017 – sabotage by striking workers, human rights commission approached – no water for more than a week – 2 weeks in some places
Dec 2017 – Major sewage leak on Uvongo Beach – Lagoon closed (Holidays) – water shortages
Jan 2018 – residents post pics of water (BROWN) on fb which Ugu labels as slanderous, however more and more residents joined the online protest...
June 2018 – disagreements between the workers and management led to pump stations and other infrastructure being sabotaged – 18 days without water

2019:
* In January The Auditor General released a statement that Ugu's financial Statements are flawed. The AG said “Ugu had failed to account for and provide evidence on how it spends money and its income”. Unauthorised spending to the tune of R243,82 million
* March 7 days no water
* free water credit has been removed (i.e. the free six kilolitres)
* Ugu asking for 22% increase in water
* Laid another complaint with Human Rights Commission (17 May)
* Protests in Boboyi – service delivery
* Port Edward 25 days no water
* Some places in Ramsgate – 7 weeks no water

Press Release:


Ugu’s Water Woes
For the last four years, Carte Blanche has received escalating complaints of persistent and prolonged water outages in the district of Ugu, stretching from Scottburgh next to Durban for over a 100km south along the KwaZulu-Natal coastline – a prime beach holiday destination. With complaints of salty and brown water or no water coming through the taps in their homes, residents at their wits’ end are engaged in a social media war with their municipality. We examine what lies behind the municipality’s apparent inability to cater for the region’s growing water demands.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf
Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


UGU Water Woes Script
UPSOUND
I live in Leisure Bay and we've had no water for probably about 10 days. This is the way we actually have to wash. As you can see the shower is not working.

No water from Ugu...

banners rest has been without water for about 3 weeks...
LINK
We've been inundated about water service delivery issues along the South Coast of KZN so we decided to take a trip down the coast.
V/O
The Ugu DISTRICT Municipality stretches from Scottburgh to Port Edward, encompassing four LOCAL municipalities. Ugu is responsible for the all water and sanitation.
V/O
First stop: Marina Beach, South of Margate...
Chantal Hartley
We haven't had water for going into 8 weeks.

CLAIRE: So you open your taps and nothing?

I open my taps and nothing.
V/O
Chantal Hartley and her family captured some rainwater in a tank during the Easter Storms. They use it sparingly.
Chantal Hartley
We boil the water, we bath in the bucket. We cook with the rain water, we wash dishes with the rain water, we don't drink the rain water, we have to buy drinking water for that.
V/O
Like Hartley, lower South Coast residents face water outages because of a broken pump in the Umtamvuna river.
DD Naidoo
During those floods we were very badly hit. And when you know those rivers came down they come down with a whole lot of debris and there was a piece of metal that came through it got into the pump and that pump obviously ceased.
V/O
DD Naidoo is Ugu’s Municipal Manager. He says the remaining pump is not enough to service the entire area, and so the administration introduced watershedding from Southbroom to Port Edward.
DD NAIDOO
So we are now pumping at less than half the capacity at Umtamvuna. And that is what the problem is.
V/O
Switching water off and on is not as simple as flicking a switch. Reservoirs need to fill up and the correct pressure reached before residents at the end of the line get water. Many areas are not getting any water at all.
V/o
At the Southern tip of the District lies Port Edward where Loraine Botha runs an Inn.
Loraine Botha
When we have got water we fill up 5l bottles of water. That's for the drinking. But for flushing the toilet we just get water out of the swimming pool, fill the bath up and we use the water over there to flush the toilets.
V/O
Living and running a business under these circumstances is not easy, and Botha says the watershedding is not working.
Loraine Botha
Last week it was a disaster. It didn't work out that well.
Dave Watson
The Umtamvuna system supplies 189,000 people with water, 28,000 households. So this is a serious... this is not just a small area, not just a small suburb.
V/O – hier moet jy net se presies wat die A-G se
Port Edward ward councillor, Dave Watson says they saw this coming – as even the Auditor General has said the municipality had regressed in terms of audit outcomes and reasonable steps were not taken to prevent unauthorised expenditure amounting to R243million.
Dave Watson
Unfortunately this is the culmination of a perfect storm that we've been anticipating for a very long time. Basically the most reasonable interpretation of Ugu is that they're a failed entity – not able to provide the services which they are contracted to do. It's actually as simple as that.
V/O
Besides the Umtamvuna system that limps along with one pump, the entire water network on the coast is aging and fails daily.
Vijay Naidoo
Claire, it's a daily occurrence. At the moment I will confidently say that there are areas in the district that have got water outages every single day.
V/O
President of the South Coast Chamber of Business and Industry, Vijay Naidoo says water interruptions is a region-wide crisis.
Vijay Naidoo
They last anything from up to a few hours to a few weeks.

In a short trip from Hibberdene to Port Shepstone we filmed four leaks in the pipeline. Currently in Uvongo a sewage pump station is not working and on Friday a major water & sewage leak was reported.
DD Naidoo
We have a lot of asbestos pipes that were used many many years ago. Now these asbestos pipes when they start breaking you you will obviously shut off the water you repair them. And when you open the water, the pressure... so you will continue having breaks on the same line for a couple days...
V/O
Naidoo says they have identified pipes that must be replaced as a priority.
DD Naidoo
The problem is that we don't have all the funding for this. But yeah we must agree with what are you saying that we do have a serious problem with pipeline replacement.
V/O
Leading water expert, Prof Anthony Turton, who lives in South Port on the South Coast believes there’s an even larger issue – salt water that entered the system at the Umzimkulu River in 2015.
Anthony Turton
When we had a very bad drought a couple of years ago that river stopped flowing and when that river stops flowing salt water goes back up the estuary, so you've got saline intrusion…. it was reticulated throughout the pipework
DD Naidoo
Obviously it backed up to such an extent where it caught us at our extraction point and that's when we extracted salt water. We stopped that immediately but now we have built a earthen berm that prevents the water from going upstream.

CLAIRE: Does that salt water not corrode infrastructure, did that have a long-lasting affect?

No it was just a couple of days.
Dave Watson
That saline solution was truly an indicator of the lack of control and the lack of duty of care.
V/O
For Naidoo urbanisation and growing water demands are much bigger contributors to pressure on the system.
DD Naidoo
There are certain rural especially in rural areas that never had water supply before. And as we proceed now we have to start reticulating water to them.
V/O
Rural KwaNzimakwe, 5 kilometres inland from Palm Beach received their long-awaited water reservoir in 2014 but it didn’t mean constant water supply.
Zola Lithuli
There's not even one year that goes past without any water issues.
V/O
Zola Lithuli and her two daughters have a tap that Zola had installed at her own cost, but they still struggle for water, daily.
Zola Lithuli
Now since it's like this we have to go fetch the water on the river. The river is very dirty and the water is brown. So we can't use it to eat or to cook or to drink, so we're struggling.
LINK
For many people in the region, tourism is their main source of income. But without water the tourists will stop coming.
Vijay Naidoo
The fewer tourists you've got it has an impact across the entire economy.
V/O
The Municipality says it is working hard to provide water for the entire district and the Bhobhoyi Water Treatment Works in the Umzimkulu river has just been upgraded.
DD Naidoo
The biggest problem is that we have an issue with finance. Government gives us a certain amount that we have to use for water infrastructure and that is really not enough. We are not denying that we have financial challenges but we have put various strategies in place – a cost containment strategy, a revenue turnaround strategy, water services strategy to reduce the costs.
V/O
The Municipality also plans to increase tariffs to raise revenue. AND they're doing away with the six free basic cubic metres to every household. For South Coast residents this means more expensive water.
Dave Watson
I could find no value, no argument, no value in the budget that meant this increase and the removal of the 6 kilolitres will make a fundamental difference to the financial viability of Ugu.
V/O
While debates around solutions rage on, residents rally to take care of tourists and each other.
Chantal Hartley
We've been blessed with the most amazing friends around that we go and shower at their houses.
Lorraine
The country club has offered people to have showers there at the country club because they've got a borehole, you see...
Dave Watson
Visitors coming down here, we make a plan, we make it happen. We may not be able to share our water, but we can certainly share our spirit and our hospitality. You know what I mean. We will get through this.


PROMO 1 11”
Regular water cuts, failing water and sewage pumps and a municipality that's struggling to keep up with the growing demand... A water crisis is threatening the livelihood of the KZN South Coast.


PROMO 2 11”
The KZN South Coast is desperate for water, but a lack of pumping capacity and aged dysfunctional infrastructure means that the current water crisis is far from over...


PROMO 3 11”
Residents of the KZN South Coast have been struggling for years with persistent and prolonged water outages, which has now culminated in a crisis affecting more than 28,000 households.

V/O The Municipality also plans to increase tariffs to raise revenue. AND they're doing away with the six free basic cubic metres to every household. For South Coast residents this means more expensive water. Dave Watson I could find no value, no argument, no value in the budget that meant this increase and the removal of the 6 kilolitres will make a fundamental difference to the financial viability of Ugu. V/O While debates around solutions rage on, residents rally to take care of tourists and each other. Chantal Hartley We've been blessed with the most amazing friends around that we go and shower at their houses. Lorraine The country club has offered people to have showers there at the country club because they've got a borehole, you see... Dave Watson Visitors coming down here, we make a plan, we make it happen. We may not be able to share our water, but we can certainly share our spirit and our hospitality. You know what I mean. We will get through this. PROMO 1 11” Regular water cuts, failing water and sewage pumps and a municipality that's struggling to keep up with the growing demand... A water crisis is threatening the livelihood of the KZN South Coast. PROMO 2 11” The KZN South Coast is desperate for water, but a lack of pumping capacity and aged dysfunctional infrastructure means that the current water crisis is far from over... PROMO 3 11” Residents of the KZN South Coast have been struggling for years with persistent and prolonged water outages, which has now culminated in a crisis affecting more than 28,000 households.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What is going on in Ugu that peope are without water repeatedly, for years on end?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche has been receiving submissions from the people of the South Coast area for several years - Ugu District Municipality covers 4 local municipalities on the KZN South Coast. The entire region has been plagued by water service delivery issues for years. As far back as 2015, residents began complaining about regular water cuts, a high number of water service interruptions and the Ugu Municipality's lack of engagement with them. Now it's time for answers. CURRENTLY Some 28 000 households which receive their water from the Umthamvuna Water Treatment Works have not had a reliable supply for the past month. According to the Ugu Municipality, the pump was damamged during the floods over Easter, but the community says these problems have been around for a long time.
metadata.Summary: TREATMENT Either start with the most dramatic case study of a business or family out of water…or link about submissions to CB -- (reading complains excerpts from the FB page and letters we have received)..Film the rest like a bit of a travelogue...show where the place is and what the importance of the area is – Gautengers know it as the beach capital of the Easter holidays…LINK – We've been watching the story closely, hundreds of complaints and we've decided to pay a visit to the KZN South Coast -- presenter driving to South Coast…Drone shots. Dave Watson / George Henderson, DA councillors who have been assisting the community for the past 4 years, by keeping people in the loop. They post daily or weekly updates on FB letting people know what's going on, where the outages are and where to find tankers with relief water, if there are any... They can outline the issues... explain the problems.. They can take us to the water reservoirs explain how they're repeatedly running dry... Visit & speak to residents and business owners about frustrations – from Hibberdene to Port Edward Anthony Turton (Or he might refer me to expert with closer knowledge) on the aging of infrastructure, the issue with saltwater in the system... Show footage of the river and pumping station Additional issues like sewage spills and infrastructure failing etc (have footage of spills and water leaks) Ugu Municipality – DD Naidoo is the Municipal Manager, but I'm not sure he will concede to an interview... So we'll doorstop the municipality Auditor General on irregularities in the Ugu financials Have footage of many water leaks on the coast Have pictures of dirty water from the taps Below are just some “highlights” - there are literally daily reports of no water on the South Coast, and of water leaks and burst pipes.
metadata.Further information: HIGHLIGHTS Experts say that salt water entered the water system during the drought in 2015 – which has corroded pipes and caused the collapse of the already aging infrastructure – Nov 2015 – complaints of salty water and brown water coming out of taps UGU issues tender for R17Million for security services for 36 months (should cover the 2 strikes and sabotage, however no-one ever saw security company anywhere) Dec 2016 – Water Crisis... lot of areas without water for more than a week – December holidays – SAMWU strike blamed Feb 2016 – places report 6 days no water Sept 2017 – Water Crisis – lack of water for more than 11 days Jul 2017 – School Holidays – water shortages – Municipality issues a statement Nov 2017 – sabotage by striking workers, human rights commission approached – no water for more than a week – 2 weeks in some places Dec 2017 – Major sewage leak on Uvongo Beach – Lagoon closed (Holidays) – water shortages Jan 2018 – residents post pics of water (BROWN) on fb which Ugu labels as slanderous, however more and more residents joined the online protest... June 2018 – disagreements between the workers and management led to pump stations and other infrastructure being sabotaged – 18 days without water 2019: * In January The Auditor General released a statement that Ugu's financial Statements are flawed. The AG said “Ugu had failed to account for and provide evidence on how it spends money and its income”. Unauthorised spending to the tune of R243,82 million * March 7 days no water * free water credit has been removed (i.e. the free six kilolitres) * Ugu asking for 22% increase in water * Laid another complaint with Human Rights Commission (17 May) * Protests in Boboyi – service delivery * Port Edward 25 days no water * Some places in Ramsgate – 7 weeks no water
